new_symbol_range_suggestions.shift_curvature_frac: dimensionless, typically between -1 and 1; values with Abs(shift_curvature_frac) of order unity allow visible threshold-surface rotation without unbounded distortion

derivation_notes: The parent assumed one sign-preserving ionic threshold-shift branch whose level dependence depended only on voltage. Here the ionic shift is re-derived to include a joint ionic-by-voltage stabilization term, representing stronger differential ionic screening of early versus late activation conformations as ionic deviation itself increases.
change_summary: A new bounded interaction term was added inside the effective half-activation shift so the ionic threshold displacement can rotate across activation quantiles rather than remaining one shared sign-preserving profile. This changes the scored mapping m_inf(V,I_cond) by making low- and high-occupancy regions respond differently to the same ionic perturbation.

assumption_audit.released_assumption: The ionic-condition effect on effective half-activation is a single sign-preserving bounded shift applied uniformly enough across sequential activation levels that one ionic shift branch describes all activation quantiles.
assumption_audit.mechanism: Ionic screening or ion-dependent state stabilization can act differently on early closed-state occupancy than on late near-permissive occupancy, causing quantile-dependent threshold movement across voltage even at steady state.
assumption_audit.parent_reduction: Taking shift_curvature_frac = 0 recovers the parent law exactly.

response_change.parent_relation: The parent maps voltage and ionic condition to activation with one ionic-condition-induced threshold shift that is monotone and sign-preserving across the full voltage range, only modestly reshaped by a bounded level-dependent factor.
response_change.child_relation: Replace the sign-preserving ionic threshold shift assumption with a state-dependent ionic effect that can differ between the activation foot and shoulder strongly enough to rotate the V-by-I threshold surface, so equal ionic changes can shift low-occupancy and high-occupancy quantiles by different amounts and potentially much less around mid-activation.
response_change.observable_effect: When I_cond is varied at fixed temperature, the voltage displacement between two ionic conditions is not approximately shared across activation quantiles: the foot may shift more than the shoulder over the sampled voltage range, producing a quantile-dependent horizontal separation that a single parent parameter set cannot match if it must keep one sign-preserving ionic shift profile.

evolution_contract.observable_signature: Across voltage sweeps at two or more ionic conditions, the horizontal separation between activation curves becomes quantile dependent: for admissible ionic deviations and voltages spanning the sigmoid foot and shoulder, low-occupancy regions can shift more strongly than upper-occupancy regions, or vice versa, instead of sharing one nearly common threshold displacement.
evolution_contract.shortcut_blocked: A single refitted parent parameter set cannot reproduce this contrast because its ionic threshold shift is constrained to the form ionic_shift_max*tanh((I_cond - I_ref)/ionic_scale)*(1 + shift_level_frac*tanh((V - V_half)/shift_voltage_scale)), where all activation levels inherit the same sign-preserving ionic branch and only one bounded voltage warp. Retuning ionic_shift_max, ionic_scale, shift_level_frac, shift_voltage_scale, or slope terms can change overall size or mild asymmetry, but cannot make the strength of level-specific warping itself grow with ionic deviation so that one quantile remains relatively anchored while another moves substantially over the same I_cond change.

evolution_plan.activation_condition: Observable when ionic deviations are large enough to engage tanh saturation partially and the sampled voltage range spans both the activation foot and shoulder, with shift_voltage_scale of order the activation width so quantile-specific displacements can be resolved.
evolution_plan.train_hidden_contrast: In training, moderate ionic contrasts already reveal unequal low- versus high-occupancy shifts; in holdout, larger but still admissible ionic deviations amplify the same threshold-surface rotation rather than introducing a new mechanism.
evolution_plan.continuation_path: Recover the parent by taking the added state-dependence amplitude to zero, restoring a sign-preserving ionic shift that varies only through the existing bounded factor.
evolution_plan.gap_statement: The current model assumes one shared ionic threshold-shift branch whose sign is fixed across activation level, so ionic condition mainly translates the activation curve with limited bounded warping; it cannot represent a stronger rotation of the activation manifold in which ionic stabilization differs materially between early and late permissive rearrangements.
evolution_plan.baseline_assumption: The ionic-condition effect on effective half-activation is a single sign-preserving bounded shift applied uniformly enough across sequential activation levels that one ionic shift branch describes all activation quantiles.
evolution_plan.scientific_mechanism: Ionic screening or ion-dependent state stabilization can act differently on early closed-state occupancy than on late near-permissive occupancy, causing quantile-dependent threshold movement across voltage even at steady state.
evolution_plan.rationale: V and I_cond vary while temperature and other conditions remain fixed. In the parent, changing I_cond produces a largely translational shift of the activation curve, with only limited bounded deformation because the ionic shift keeps one sign across voltage. A realistic next refinement is to relax that idealization and allow stronger level-specific ionic stabilization of sequential closed-to-permissive occupancies. Then the horizontal separation between two ionic conditions becomes activation-level dependent: for example, the low-activation foot can move substantially while the upper shoulder moves weakly over the same ionic change, or vice versa. This is a changed target mapping m_inf(V,I_cond), not merely an auxiliary reinterpretation. The contrast is scientifically admissible when the voltage sweep covers a broad enough portion of the sigmoid and ionic deviations are sufficient to reveal differential screening/stabilization across sequential conformations. A single refitted parent parameter set cannot reproduce an arbitrary rotated threshold surface because its ionic shift branch is constrained to one sign-preserving bounded profile across activation level; it can broaden or narrow and modestly bend, but not supply independently stronger ionic displacement at one activation quantile while keeping another nearly anchored across the same I_cond range.

selected_embedding_pattern.description: Make one process depend jointly on two declared quantities.

scenario_text: A voltage-clamp experiment samples membrane potential while temperature and ionic conditions remain fixed. The target is the steady fraction of activation gates occupying the permissive conformation in a voltage-sensitive neuronal ion channel. Voltage-dependent changes in conformational occupancy produce a bounded sigmoidal response. Transient gating and channel inactivation are excluded from the baseline question.
